title: The Sunday Read: ‘The Moral Crisis of America’s Doctors’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档探讨设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里做DJ时，你每天晚上也会带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，并将DJ台

sentences.en: into this living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个由精美的50年历史艺术品组成的、生动的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Eyal Press, and I'm a contributor to The New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是埃亚尔·普雷斯，《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: A few years ago, I got this email from a high-ranking official at a hospital that sent me down a rabbit hole.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我收到了一家医院高级官员发来的电子邮件，这让我陷入了一个长期的追查。

sentences.en: The Times had just published an excerpt from a book of mine called Dirty Work, which examines low-wage, low-status workers in places like the prison system
sentences.zh: 《时报》刚刚发表了我的一本书的节选，书名叫《肮脏的工作》，该书审视了诸如监狱系统

sentences.en: and the meatpacking industry.
sentences.zh: 和肉类加工行业中那些低薪、低地位的工人。

sentences.en: The book looked not only at the economic challenges these workers face, but also at the moral dilemmas they experience doing their jobs, how it can go against their core values.
sentences.zh: 这本书不仅关注这些工人所面临的经济挑战，还关注他们在工作中体验到的道德困境，以及这些困境如何违背他们的核心价值观。

sentences.en: This hospital official had read my excerpt, and they wrote to me, saying there's another group I should look into that might also fit into the topic of dirty work.
sentences.zh: 这位医院官员读了我的节选后写信给我，说我应该调查另一个可能也符合肮脏工作主题的群体。

sentences.en: A group of workers who were going through dilemmas as wrenching as those of Border Patrol agents and slaughterhouse workers.
sentences.zh: 这是一群经历着与边境巡逻人员和屠宰场工人同样痛苦困境的劳动者。

sentences.en: And they were talking about doctors.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的是医生。

sentences.en: At first, I was skeptical.
sentences.zh: 起初，我是持怀疑态度的。

sentences.en: Like, really?
sentences.zh: 心想，真的吗？

sentences.en: Physicians who are earning $200,000 salaries and have degrees from Harvard and NYU are experiencing this same level of moral crisis?
sentences.zh: 拿着20万美元年薪、拥有哈佛和纽约大学学位内科医生，也在经历同样水平的道德危机吗？

sentences.en: But I gave this person a call, and that's where this Sunday read begins.
sentences.zh: 但我给这个人打了个电话，这就是这篇周日深度阅读的开始。

sentences.en: The story that I think is familiar to people is that doctors are burning out.
sentences.zh: 我认为大家都很熟悉的一种说法是，医生正在精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They're working too hard, they're seeing too much suffering, and it's wearing on them over long hours and sleepless nights, especially since the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 他们工作太辛苦，目睹了太多的痛苦，漫长的工作时间和不眠之夜正在消磨他们，尤其是大流行以来更是如此。

sentences.en: But that's only part of the story.
sentences.zh: 但这只是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: In this piece for the magazine, I wrote about the ethical quandaries that physicians are finding themselves in as they try to provide care in an American medical system
sentences.zh: 在这篇为杂志撰写的文章中，我写到了内科医生们在试图提供医疗服务时所陷入的伦理困境，而美国的医疗系统

sentences.en: that's increasingly driven by profit.
sentences.zh: 正日益被利润所驱动。

sentences.en: You see it playing out across the country.
sentences.zh: 你可以在全国各地看到这种现象的上演。

sentences.en: Pediatric treatment is being whittled down because it's not a moneymaker.
sentences.zh: 儿科治疗正在被削减，因为它不赚钱。

sentences.en: Primary care practices are getting bought up by CVS and Amazon.
sentences.zh: 初级保健诊所正被CVS和亚马逊收购。

sentences.en: And that's left doctors feeling controlled and pressured to do things that go against their own medical ethics.
sentences.zh: 这使得医生们感到被控制，并被迫去做违背他们自身医学伦理的事情。

sentences.en: I spoke with dozens of physicians who said they're finding themselves in extremely uncomfortable situations, like having a seven-minute window to see patients,
sentences.zh: 我采访了数十名医生，他们表示自己正处于极其尴尬的境地，比如只有七分钟的时间来看诊，

sentences.en: or being forced to switch a patient to a new medication because that's what their insurance will cover, even when it's dangerous to do that,
sentences.zh: 或者被迫为患者更换新药，因为那是他们的保险能够报销的，即使这样做很危险，

sentences.en: or having a patient come to them in tears over an expensive hospital bill that they then have to explain.
sentences.zh: 或者有患者哭着来找他们询问昂贵的医院账单，而他们不得不对此进行解释。

sentences.en: One provider became emotional, telling me how, at her practice, she's so squeezed for time that she can't even sit by a patient's side while they're dying.
sentences.zh: 一名医护人员情绪激动地告诉我，在她的诊所里，她的时间被压榨得如此厉害，以至于在病人垂死时，她甚至无法坐在病床边。

sentences.en: And so, more and more, doctors are feeling that they're the face of a system they can't morally defend.
sentences.zh: 因此，越来越多的医生感到自己成了一个他们在道德上无法辩护的系统的门面。

sentences.en: They've come to feel like scapegoats for the system's inequities.
sentences.zh: 他们开始觉得自己成了系统不公的替罪羊。

sentences.en: And, in some instances, one source told me, they feel that they are acting as the instruments of a system they don't even believe in anymore.
sentences.zh: 而在某些情况下，一位消息人士告诉我，他们觉得自己正在充当一个他们甚至不再相信的系统的工具。

sentences.en: Throughout my reporting, all of the doctors I spoke with took pains to say, look, this concerns me primarily because of what it means for my patients, not what it means for me.
sentences.zh: 在我的整个采访过程中，所有与我交谈过的医生都煞费苦心地表示，听着，这主要关乎它对我的患者意味着什么，而不是对意味着我什么。

sentences.en: But doctors also feel like victims of the system, and the numbers very much confirm this, whether it's the alarming suicide rate among physicians, or the number of doctors
sentences.zh: 但医生们也觉得自己是这个系统的受害者，数字充分证实了这一点，无论是医生中惊人的自杀率，还是那些

sentences.en: who are considering quitting and pursuing something else.
sentences.zh: 正考虑辞职并追求别的事业的医生数量。

sentences.en: Since my article came out,
sentences.zh: 自从我的文章发表以来，

sentences.en: I've been flooded with correspondence from doctors, just letter after letter from people telling me they've considered quitting, or they are quitting, or they left the country
sentences.zh: 我收到了大量的医生来信，一封又一封的信件倾诉着他们曾考虑辞职、正在辞职，或者已经离开这个国家

sentences.en: to go practice medicine in New Zealand or Canada.
sentences.zh: 去新西兰或加拿大行医。

sentences.en: I haven't gotten a single letter from a doctor saying, the system is just fine.
sentences.zh: 我没有收到哪怕一封来自医生的信说，这个系统一切都好。

sentences.en: In fact, most have told me, you've scratched the surface of how bad things really are, and how bad they're going to get.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数人告诉我，你只是触及了事情究竟有多糟以及未来会有多糟的冰山一角。

sentences.en: So here's my article,
sentences.zh: 这就是我的文章，

sentences.en: The Moral Crisis of America's Doctors, read by Eduardo Ballerini.
sentences.zh: 《美国医生的道德危机》，由爱德华多·巴勒里尼为您朗读。

sentences.en: Some years ago, a psychiatrist named Wendy Dean read an article about a physician who died by suicide.
sentences.zh: 几年前，一位名叫温迪·迪恩的精神病学家读到了一篇关于一名自杀身亡的医生的文章。

sentences.en: Such deaths were distressingly common, she discovered.
sentences.zh: 她发现，此类死亡事件极其普遍且令人痛心。

sentences.en: The suicide rate among doctors appeared to be even higher than the rate among active military members, a notion that startled Dean, who was then working as an administrator
sentences.zh: 医生的自杀率似乎甚至高于现役军人，这个概念让迪恩感到震惊，当时她在马里兰州的一个美国

sentences.en: at a U.S.
sentences.zh: 陆军

sentences.en: Army medical research center in Maryland.
sentences.zh: 医学研究中心担任行政人员。

sentences.en: Dean started asking the physicians she knew how they felt about their jobs, and many of them confided that they were struggling.
sentences.zh: 迪恩开始向她认识的医生询问他们对工作的感受，许多人吐露说他们正在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: Some complained that they didn't have enough time to talk to their patients because they were too busy filling out electronic medical records.
sentences.zh: 有些人抱怨他们没有足够的时间和病人交谈，因为他们太忙于填写电子病历。

sentences.en: Others bemoaned having to fight with insurers about whether a person with a serious illness would be pre-approved for medication.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则感叹不得不与保险公司争论患有重病的患者是否能预先获得药物批准。

sentences.en: The doctors Dean surveyed were deeply committed to the medical profession.
sentences.zh: 迪恩调查的医生对医疗行业有着极高的忠诚度。

sentences.en: But many of them were frustrated and unhappy, she sensed, not because they were burned out from working too hard, but because the health care system made it so difficult
sentences.zh: 但她感觉到，他们中的许多人感到沮丧和不快乐，不是因为工作太累而精疲力竭，而是因为医疗保健系统使得

sentences.en: to care for their patients.
sentences.zh: 照顾病人变得如此困难。

sentences.en: In July 2018,
Dean published an essay with Simon G.
sentences.zh: 迪恩与整形和重建外科医生西蒙·G·

sentences.en: Talbot, a plastic and reconstructive surgeon, that argued that many physicians were suffering from a condition known as moral injury.
sentences.zh: 塔尔博特发表了一篇论文，论证了许多医生正在遭受一种被称为道德损伤的病症之苦。

sentences.en: Military psychiatrists used the term to describe an emotional wound sustained when, in the course of fulfilling their duties, soldiers witnessed or committed acts, raiding a home,
sentences.zh: 军事精神病学家用这个术语来描述一种情感创伤，当士兵在履行职责的过程中目睹或实施了诸如搜查房屋、

sentences.en: killing a non-combatant, that transgressed their core values.
sentences.zh: 杀死非战斗人员等违背其核心价值观的行为时，便会受到这种创伤。

sentences.en: Doctors on the front lines of America's profit-driven health care system were also susceptible to such wounds,
sentences.zh: 处于美国以利润为导向的医疗保健系统最前沿的医生也同样容易受到此类创伤，

sentences.en: Dean and Talbot submitted, as the demands of administrators, hospital executives, and insurers forced them to stray from the ethical principles that were supposed
sentences.zh: 迪恩和塔尔博特指出，因为行政人员、医院高管和保险公司的要求迫使他们偏离了本应

sentences.en: to govern their profession.
sentences.zh: 指导他们职业生涯的道德原则。

sentences.en: The pull of these forces left many doctors anguished and distraught, caught between the Hippocratic oath and the realities of making a profit from people at their sickest
sentences.zh: 这些力量的拉扯使许多医生感到痛苦和心碎，在希波克拉底誓言与从病得最重、最脆弱的人身上

sentences.en: and most vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 牟利的现实之间苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: The article was published on STAT, a medical news website with a modest readership.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章发表在STAT上，这是一个读者群不大的医学新闻网站。

sentences.en: To Dean's surprise, it quickly went viral.
sentences.zh: 令迪恩惊讶的是，它迅速在网上疯传。

sentences.en: Doctors and nurses started reaching out to Dean to tell her how much the article spoke to them.
sentences.zh: 医生和护士开始联系迪恩，告诉她这篇文章多么契合他们的心声。

sentences.en: It went everywhere,
sentences.zh: 它传到了各处，

sentences.en: Dean told me when I visited her last March in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, where she now lives.
sentences.zh: 去年3月我去宾夕法尼亚州卡莱尔拜访她时，她对我说，她现在就住在那里。

sentences.en: By the time we met, the distress among medical professionals had reached alarming levels.
sentences.zh: 当我们见面时，医疗专业人员中的痛苦情绪已经达到了令人震惊的水平。

sentences.en: One survey found that nearly one in five health care workers had quit their job since the start of the pandemic, and that an additional 31% had considered leaving.
sentences.zh: 一项调查发现，自大流行开始以来，近五分之一的医护人员已经辞职，另有31%的人考虑过离开。

sentences.en: Professional organizations like National Nurses United, the largest group of registered nurses in the country had begun referring to moral injury and moral distress in pamphlets
sentences.zh: 像全美护士联合会（全国最大的注册护士群体）这样的专业组织，已经开始在小册子

sentences.en: and news releases.
sentences.zh: 和新闻稿中提及道德损伤和道德困扰。

sentences.en: Mona Massoud, a psychiatrist who established a support line for doctors shortly after the pandemic began, recalls being struck by how clinicians reacted
sentences.zh: 莫娜·马苏德是一名精神病学家，在大流行开始后不久为医生建立了一条支持热线，她回忆说，当她提到这个词时，

sentences.en: when she mentioned the term.
sentences.zh: 临床医生的反应让她印象深刻。

sentences.en: I remember all these physicians were like, wow, that is what I was looking for, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说道，我记得所有这些医生都觉得，哇，这正是我一直在寻找的。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.en: Dean's essay caught my eye, too, because I spent much of the previous few years reporting on moral injury, interviewing workers in menial occupations whose jobs
sentences.zh: 迪恩的文章也吸引了我的目光，因为在过去的几年里，我花了很多时间报道道德损伤，采访了那些工作在道德上

sentences.en: were ethically compromising.
sentences.zh: 会带来妥协的低微职业的工人。

sentences.en: I spoke to prison guards who patrolled the wards of violent penitentiaries, undocumented immigrants who toiled on the kill floors of industrial slaughterhouses, and roustabouts
sentences.zh: 我采访过在暴力监狱病房巡逻的狱警、在工业屠宰场屠宰车间辛勤劳作的无证移民，以及在化石燃料行业的海上钻井平台上

sentences.en: who worked on offshore rigs in the fossil fuel industry.
sentences.zh: 工作的零工。

sentences.en: Many of these workers were hesitant to talk or be identified, knowing how easily they could be replaced by someone else.
sentences.zh: 这些工人大多对开口说话或暴露身份感到犹豫，因为他们知道自己是多么容易被别人取代。

sentences.en: Compared with them, physicians were privileged, earning six-figure salaries and doing prestigious jobs that spared them from the drudgery endured by so many other members
sentences.zh: 与他们相比，医生是享有特权的，拿着六位数的薪水，从事着崇高的工作，使他们免于医疗行业中许多其他成员

sentences.en: of the labor force, including nurses and custodial workers in the healthcare industry.
sentences.zh: （包括护士和工勤人员）所忍受的苦差事。

sentences.en: But in recent years, despite the esteem associated with their profession, many physicians have found themselves subjected to practices more commonly associated with manual labors
sentences.zh: 但近年来，尽管他们的职业备受尊崇，许多医生发现自己受到的对待更类似于汽车厂和亚马逊仓库里的

sentences.en: in auto plants and Amazon warehouses, like having their productivity tracked on an hourly basis and being pressured by management to work faster.
sentences.zh: 体力劳动者，比如按小时追踪生产力，以及受到管理层的催促以加快工作速度。

sentences.en: Because doctors are highly skilled professionals who are not so easy to replace, I assumed that they would not be as reluctant to discuss the distressing conditions at their jobs
sentences.zh: 由于医生是并非那么容易被取代的高技能专业人员，我原以为他们在讨论工作中的痛苦状况时，不会像我

sentences.en: as the low-wage workers
sentences.zh: 采访过的低薪工人那样

sentences.en: I'd interviewed.
sentences.zh: 感到有所顾忌。

sentences.en: But the physicians I contacted were afraid to talk openly.
sentences.zh: 但我联系的医生们却害怕公开谈论。

sentences.en: I have since reconsidered this and do not feel this is something I can do right now, one doctor wrote to me.
sentences.zh: 一位医生写信给我：我后来重新考虑了，觉得这不是我现在能做的事情。

sentences.en: Another texted, we'll need to be anon.
sentences.zh: 另一位发短信说，我们需要匿名。

sentences.en: Some sources I tried to reach had signed non-disclosure agreements that prohibited them from speaking to the media without permission.
sentences.zh: 我试图联系的一些消息来源签署了保密协议，禁止他们在没有许可的情况下向媒体发言。

sentences.en: Others worried they could be disciplined or fired if they angered their employers, a concern that seems particularly well-founded in the growing swath of the healthcare system
sentences.zh: 另一些人则担心，如果惹恼了雇主，他们可能会受到纪律处分或被解雇，在医疗保健系统中越来越多被私私募股权公司

sentences.en: that has been taken over by private equity firMs.
sentences.zh: 接管的领域，这种担忧似乎尤为合理。

sentences.en: In March 2020, an emergency room doctor named Ming Lin was removed from the rotation at his hospital after airing concerns about its COVID-19 safety protocols.
sentences.zh: 2020年3月，一名名叫明·林的急诊室医生因公开对医院的COVID-19安全协议表示担忧而被撤出值班轮换。

sentences.en: Lin worked at St. Joseph Medical Center in Bellingham, Washington, but his actual employer was Team Health, a company owned by the Blackstone Group.
sentences.zh: 林在华盛顿州贝灵厄姆的圣约瑟夫医疗中心工作，但他真正的雇主是黑石集团旗下的Team Health公司。

sentences.en: ER doctors have found themselves at the forefront of these trends as more and more hospitals have outsourced the staffing in emergency departments in order to cut costs.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的医院将急诊部门的 staffing 外包以削减成本，急诊室医生发现自己正处于这些趋势的最前沿。

sentences.en: A 2013 study by Robert McNamara, the chairman of the Emergency Medicine Department at Temple University in Philadelphia, found that 62% of emergency physicians in the United States
sentences.zh: 费城天普大学急诊医学系主任罗伯特·麦克纳马拉2013年的一项研究发现，美国62%的急诊医生

sentences.en: could be fired without due process.
sentences.zh: 可以在没有正当程序的情况下被解雇。

sentences.en: Nearly 20% of the 389 ER doctors surveyed said they had been threatened for raising quality of care concerns and pressured to make decisions based on financial considerations
sentences.zh: 在接受调查的389名急诊医生中，近20%的人表示，他们曾因提出护理质量问题而遭到威胁，并被施压要求根据可能会损害患者利益的

sentences.en: that could be detrimental to the people in their care, like being pushed to discharge Medicare and Medicaid patients or being encouraged to order more testing than necessary.
sentences.zh: 财务考虑做出决定，例如被催促让医疗保险和医疗补助患者出院，或者被鼓励进行不必要的过多检查。

sentences.en: In another study, more than 70% of emergency physicians agreed that the corporatization of their field has had a negative or strongly negative impact on the quality of care
sentences.zh: 在另一项研究中，超过70%的急诊医生认同，他们这一领域的企业化对护理质量

sentences.en: and on their own job satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 以及他们自己的工作满意度产生了消极或非常消极的影响。

sentences.en: There are, of course, plenty of doctors who like what they do and feel no need to speak out.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有很多医生喜欢他们的工作，觉得没有必要发声。

sentences.en: Clinicians in high-paying specialties like orthopedics and plastic surgery are doing just fine, thank you, one physician I know joked.

sentences.en: who chose to become doctors for altruistic reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于利他主义原因而选择成为医生的人。

sentences.en: They didn't quit because they don't like medicine, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，他们辞职不是因为不喜欢医学。

sentences.en: They were both wonderful physicians.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都是极好的医生。

sentences.en: And even running direct care practices, doctors cannot fully escape the frustrations and injustices of the health care system.
sentences.zh: 而且即使经营直接护理诊所，医生也无法完全逃避医疗保健系统的挫折和不公。

sentences.zh: 几个月前，

sentences.zh: 格拉尼塔告诉我，一名患者因溃疡药产生严重过敏反应而来到她这里，他的保险公司让他换了这种药，因为不再报销他

sentences.en: he'd been taking.
sentences.zh: 一直在服用的药物。

sentences.en: Granita told me she had called her patients insurer every week as his condition deteriorated.
sentences.zh: 格拉尼塔告诉我，随着患者病情的恶化，她每周都给患者的保险公司打电话。

sentences.en: When she finally got through, she was told they needed
sentences.zh: 当她终于打通时，被告知他们需要

sentences.en: 30 days to process the appeal.
sentences.zh: 30天来处理申诉。

sentences.en: Granita was livid.
sentences.zh: 格拉尼塔气疯了。

sentences.en: They are literally putting this patient in danger.
sentences.zh: 他们简直是将这位患者置于危险之中。

sentences.en: It is sick, she said.
sentences.zh: 这太变态了，她说。

sentences.en: This is sick medical care.
